```plato

    //==
    // # Dimensional lifts and symmetry
    //
    // Building a spatial shape out of a planar one, and folding a shape onto itself.
    // Deliberately split into a VALUE half and a DOMAIN half so both stay under the
    // same portability discipline as the primitives below — no lambdas, no field
    // values, only points and numbers. Extrusion is a value operator: the caller
    // samples the planar source at the point's own XY and hands the distance here.
    // Revolution and mirroring are domain operators: they map the query position and
    // the caller samples the source at the mapped point.

    // The extruded distance: a planar shape swept along Z from -halfHeight to
    // +halfHeight. planarDistance is the source's distance at (p.X, p.Y) and z is
    // p.Z. Exact wherever the planar distance is, except in the wedge outside a rim
    // where the wall and cap meet, which is a lower bound — the two constraints are
    // combined, not measured jointly. (IQ: opExtrusion.)
    ExtrudedDistance(planarDistance: Number, z: Number, halfHeight: Number): Number {
        var w = Vector2D(planarDistance, z.Abs - halfHeight);
        return w.X.Max(w.Y).Min(0.0)
             + Vector2D(w.X.Max(0.0), w.Y.Max(0.0)).Magnitude;
    }
```
